content.value_statement: TypeScript teams often write comments that repeat types or miss important behavior. This skill guides focused JSDoc for APIs, examples, errors, and maintenance notes.
actual_capabilities: Explains core JSDoc syntax for TypeScript functions, classes, and services.
Shows when to document public APIs, internal helpers, and complex behavior.
Guides documentation for nested object parameters and generic functions.
Identifies redundant comments that duplicate TypeScript type information.
limitations: Does not run documentation generators or validate rendered documentation output.
Does not modify files unless the agent applies the guidance separately.
Does not replace project-specific documentation standards or review policies.
Focuses on TypeScript JSDoc, not broad technical writing strategy.

use_cases.title: Document Public Library APIs
use_cases.description: Create clear JSDoc for exported functions, classes, and interfaces before release.

use_cases.title: Clarify Complex Application Code
use_cases.description: Add comments that explain retries, caching, errors, side effects, and usage constraints.

use_cases.title: Review Comment Quality
use_cases.description: Remove redundant comments and keep documentation focused on behavior and intent.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic JSDoc
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner documentation for a clear function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add concise JSDoc to this TypeScript function. Focus on purpose, parameters, return value, and any important edge case.

prompt_templates.title: Document Public API
prompt_templates.scenario: Public module or shared service documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this exported TypeScript API and write JSDoc that explains behavior, errors, and one practical usage example.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Existing Comments
prompt_templates.scenario: Refine comments that duplicate type information.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these JSDoc comments for redundancy. Keep only information that explains intent, constraints, side effects, or usage.

prompt_templates.title: Design Documentation Standard
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced team guidance for consistent JSDoc.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TypeScript JSDoc standard for this codebase. Include required tags, optional tags, anti-patterns, and review criteria.

output_examples.input: A public authentication service method with login errors and retry behavior.
output_examples.output: The result explains the service purpose, expected credentials, possible authentication and network errors, and a short usage example.

output_examples.input: A generic helper that removes duplicate items from an array.
output_examples.output: The result documents the type parameter, uniqueness rule, optional identifier function, and returned array behavior.

output_examples.input: A simple formatter with comments that repeat TypeScript types.
output_examples.output: The result recommends removing redundant parameter descriptions and keeping only useful display intent or examples.

best_practices: Document public APIs, exported modules, complex behavior, errors, and stable usage contracts.
Use JSDoc to explain why code behaves a certain way, not only what the types show.
Keep examples current when behavior, side effects, performance, or error conditions change.
anti_patterns: Do not repeat TypeScript type information without adding useful context.
Do not document unstable implementation details that may change during refactoring.
Do not add long comments to obvious helpers when names and types already explain behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill generate JSDoc for TypeScript code?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides an AI agent to write concise JSDoc that explains behavior, usage, errors, and examples.

faq.question: Does it support generic functions?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers @template usage and explains how type parameters affect inputs, outputs, and behavior.

faq.question: Can it document React components?
faq.answer: Yes. The reference includes component prop documentation and examples for editable component behavior.

faq.question: Will it run commands or access external services?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation guidance stored in Markdown files and does not include executable scripts.

faq.question: How does it avoid redundant comments?
faq.answer: It recommends skipping comments that only restate TypeScript types and function names.

faq.question: Is it suitable for private codebases?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide documentation style, but users should still follow internal review and confidentiality rules.
